chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya'qub ibn Zayd from Mansur from a man from Sharik, who raised it, saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When it is the Day of Judgment, Fatimah (peace be upon her) will come surrounded by the women of her family. It will be said to her, 'Enter Paradise,' but she will say, 'I will not enter until I know what was done to my children after me.' It will be said to her, 'Look in the heart of the Resurrection,' and she will look at al-Husayn (peace be upon him) standing without a head. She will cry out a cry, and I will cry out for her cry, and the angels will cry out for her cry. At that, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will become angry and will order a fire called Hab-hab, which has been kindled for a thousand years until it turned black, into which no breath will ever enter and from which no sorrow will ever escape. It will be said, 'Gather those who killed al-Husayn and carried the Quran,' so she will gather them. When they are in her pouch, she will groan and they will groan with her, she will gasp and they will gasp with her, she will sigh and they will sigh with her. They will speak with smooth, eloquent tongues, 'O our Lord, why did You decree Hell for us before the idolaters?' Then the answer will come from Allah, the Exalted, that 'Those who know are not like those who do not know.'

key_terms.حَوْصَلَه: Pouch or bag (metaphorical container for the souls/killers)
key_terms.هَبْهَب: Hab-hab (a specific name for a fire in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What happens to Fatimah (peace be upon her) on the Day of Judgment regarding her entry to Paradise and the fate of Imam Husayn's killers?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the profound intercession of Fatimah al-Zahra (a.s.), whose grief over the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.) serves as the catalyst for divine anger and the specific punishment of his killers. The text emphasizes that the severity of their punishment stems not merely from the act of killing, but from their failure to recognize the truth despite having knowledge, distinguishing them from the ignorant idolaters. This underscores the Shia theological principle that 'knowledge' (ma'rifah) carries greater weight than mere belief or action in the context of justice.
